subject: Duplicate charge on invoice #4411
body: We were billed twice for March. Please refund the extra charge to the original card.

subject: Credit note needed for cancelled seats
body: We reduced from 40 seats to 25 on 3 February but the invoice still shows 40. Please issue a credit note for the difference.
label: billing

subject: Change of payment method
body: Our finance team has moved banks. Please switch the direct debit for account ACME-8842 to the new mandate we submitted through the portal.
label: billing

subject: RE: RE: Invoice query - March statement
body:
Hi Jane,

Thanks for coming back to me so quickly, and apologies for the slow reply -- I was out at a conference most of last week.

I have been through the March statement line by line with our accounts payable team. Lines 1 through 7 all reconcile against our purchase order. The issue is line 8, "Additional API capacity", at 1,240.00. We never ordered additional capacity and I cannot find any approval for it on our side.

Could you either point me at the authorisation, or drop that line and reissue? Happy to pay the rest of the statement in the meantime so it does not go overdue.

Best regards,
John Doe
Financial Controller, Acme Corp

> On 14 March, Jane Smith wrote:
> Hi John, the March statement went out on the 1st. Let me know if
> anything looks wrong and I will take a look.

subject: Annual invoice - PO number required before we can pay
body:
Good morning,

Hope you are well.

We have received the annual renewal invoice (ref INV-2291) but our purchase ledger will reject it because it does not carry a PO number. Our system requires one on the face of the invoice for anything above 10,000.

The PO is 4500128833. Could you reissue with that quoted, and resend to payables at our shared finance mailbox rather than to me directly? That will get it into the approval queue much faster.

Thanks in advance,
Priya Patel
Accounts Payable, Northwind Trading

--
This message and any attachments are confidential.
label: billing

subject: Moving to annual billing before renewal
body:
Hello,

Following our call on Tuesday I wanted to put this in writing.

We currently pay monthly. Before the renewal date in June we would like to switch to annual billing in advance, partly for the discount and partly because monthly invoices create a lot of noise in our ledger.

Two questions:
1. What is the annual rate for our current tier at 60 seats?
2. If we switch mid-term, do you pro-rate the months already paid or does the annual term start fresh?

If the numbers work we would want the paperwork done before the end of the quarter.

Kind regards,
Tomas Berg
Operations Director, Globex Industries
label: billing

subject: Something looks off this month
body: The amount that left our account on the 1st was about four hundred more than it usually is. Nothing changed on our side that I know of. Can someone have a look and tell me what the difference is?
label: billing

subject: #support thread
body: hi -- we got a letter saying the card on file was declined and the service will stop in 7 days. the card was replaced in january, i thought we updated it. what do you need from us to sort this before it cuts off?
label: billing

subject: Urgent: system access suspended
body: Our whole team has lost access this morning and the login page shows an error. I called the helpdesk and they said it is not a fault -- the account is suspended because the November payment did not go through. Nobody told us it had failed. Please tell us what is outstanding so we can clear it and get switched back on.
label: billing

subject: Overcharged for the security add-on we never enabled
body: The line item 'Threat Monitoring' has been on our invoice for five months at 210 a month. We have never switched that module on -- the toggle in the admin console is still off. This is not a complaint about the product, it is a complaint about being charged for it. We would like the five months refunded.
label: billing

subject: 500 errors from the API since 09:00
body: Every request to /v1/orders returns HTTP 500. Our production integration is broken and has been for about forty minutes.
label: technical

subject: Webhook deliveries stopped
body: No webhook has been delivered to our endpoint since 02:14 UTC. Our endpoint is up and returns 200 to manual test posts. The delivery log in your dashboard shows no attempts at all after that timestamp.
label: technical

subject: CSV export produces corrupted file
body: Exporting more than about 50,000 rows produces a CSV that will not open -- the file is truncated mid-row. Under 50,000 rows it works fine. Reproducible every time on the Reports screen.
label: technical

subject: RE: Intermittent timeouts - more detail as requested
body:
Hi,

Following up on ticket 88213 with the detail your engineer asked for.

The timeouts happen in bursts, roughly every 90 minutes, and last 3 to 5 minutes. During a burst about one request in four fails; the rest are normal. Outside a burst we see nothing at all.

We have checked from our side: no correlation with our deploy times, no change in our request volume, and our own upstream monitoring is clean throughout. We have captured request IDs from a burst this morning between 10:42 and 10:46 and attached them.

One thing that might matter -- it started the same week you moved us to the new cluster.

Thanks,
Mark Olsen
Platform Engineering, Initech
label: technical

subject: Search returns nothing for hyphenated terms
body:
Hello support,

Reporting something our team hit repeatedly this week.

If a customer name contains a hyphen -- "Smith-Jones" for example -- searching for it returns zero results. Searching for "Smith" alone finds the record fine, and so does "Jones". Only the hyphenated form fails.

I would call this a bug rather than a limitation, because the record clearly exists and the exact string is what is stored. But if it is intended behaviour then the search box badly needs to say so, because three people here assumed the customer had been deleted.

Let me know which it is and whether there is a workaround in the meantime.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Operations, Contoso Ltd
label: technical

subject: #help thread
body: the blue button on the invoice screen does nothing now. it used to open the print preview. nothing happens at all, no spinner, no message. started some time after yesterday afternoon. three of us on different machines, same thing.
label: technical

subject: Numbers on the dashboard do not match the export
body: The summary tile says 1,284 active records. If I export the same view and count the rows I get 1,301. The seventeen that are missing from the tile all seem to have been created in the last day or so. Which of the two is right?
label: technical

subject: RE: Invoice #7781 - PDF will not download
body: This is about the invoice screen rather than the invoice itself -- the amount is correct and we are not disputing it. Clicking 'Download PDF' returns a page that says 'An unexpected error occurred, reference 0x8004'. It happens for every invoice in the list, not just this one, and for every user we have tried.
label: technical

subject: Possible security issue - users seeing a blank screen after login
body: Raising this as security in case it is one, though I suspect it is not. Since this morning some users get a completely blank page after signing in. The session seems valid because refreshing the page eventually loads. No data is exposed, nothing is leaking, it just fails to render. Feel free to reclassify.
label: technical

subject: Contract says 99.9% - we were well under that
body: I am quoting the agreement here but this is not a legal complaint, at least not yet. Your status page shows four separate outages last month totalling just over six hours, which is nowhere near the uptime in our agreement. What I actually want to know is what went wrong and what has changed so it does not repeat. The credits can wait.
label: technical

subject: Enterprise pricing for 400 seats
body: We are evaluating vendors and would like a quote and a draft contract for 400 seats, plus whatever volume discount applies at that level.
label: sales

subject: Upgrade from Professional to Enterprise
body: We are on the Professional plan and want to move to Enterprise from the start of next quarter. Could you send the price difference and what the upgrade involves?
label: sales

subject: Following up after the demo on Thursday
body:
Hi Jane,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Thursday -- it was useful, and the reporting module was better than I expected.

I have talked it over internally. We are shortlisting two vendors and you are one of them. Before we go further I need a few things in writing so I can put them to our steering group on the 28th:

- Indicative pricing at 150 and at 250 seats
- What the implementation timeline looks like realistically
- Whether the sandbox can be extended past the 14 days, since our evaluation will run longer than that

I should be straight with you that price is not the deciding factor here, but it does have to be defensible.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Head of Operations, Umbrella Retail
label: sales

subject: Order form - a few changes before signature
body:
Good afternoon,

We are close. Our legal team has been through the order form and has three changes they want before we sign:

1. The auto-renewal notice period moved from 90 days to 30.
2. A cap on the annual uplift, currently uncapped. We would accept CPI plus 2%.
3. Removal of the clause allowing you to use our name in marketing without prior approval.

None of these are dealbreakers individually but the uplift cap matters most to us. If you can turn these round this week we can still sign inside the quarter.

Regards,
Daniel Fischer
Procurement Lead, Vandelay Group
label: sales

subject: Question before we commit
body: We have been running on the free tier for about two months and it is doing what we hoped. There are now eleven of us using it rather than the two who started. What does it look like to put this on a proper footing for a team our size, and what would that cost?
label: sales

subject: Comparing options for next year's budget
body: I am putting together next year's budget and need a realistic figure for your product for a team that will probably grow from 30 to about 50 people. I do not need a formal document yet, just something defensible enough to put in a spreadsheet. Who should I talk to?
label: sales

subject: website chat transcript
body: visitor: hi, we're a 12 person agency, do you do anything for teams that size or is it all enterprise? / visitor: mainly wondering about cost before i get my director involved
label: sales

subject: Invoice for the trial period?
body: We received something that looks like an invoice for the trial, which surprised us since we understood the 30 days were free. Before I send it to finance -- is this actually a quote for what we would pay if we continue? If so we are interested, but I want to be clear which it is, and what the committed term would be.
label: sales

subject: Our contract is up and we are considering leaving
body: Our term ends on 30 June. I will be honest, we have been approached by a competitor with a noticeably lower number, and the board has asked me to justify staying. I am not trying to threaten anyone -- I would rather stay. But I need something I can take to them. What can you do on price for a three year commitment?
label: sales

subject: Bug in your pricing calculator
body: Your website calculator gives a different figure depending on whether I pick the seats first or the term first -- about 900 apart for the same configuration. I mention it mainly because I need to know which number is real, since I am building a business case on it. Which is the correct price for 80 seats on a two year term?
label: sales

subject: DPA counter-signature required
body: Our counsel requires the data processing agreement amended under Article 28 and counter-signed before we can proceed to production.
label: legal

subject: Notice of trademark concern
body: We act for Northwind Trading. Our client's registered mark is being used in your product documentation in a manner likely to cause confusion. We ask that the usage be withdrawn within 21 days.
label: legal

subject: RE: Master services agreement - redlines attached
body:
Dear Jane,

Please find attached our redlines to the draft MSA circulated on 4 May.

The substantive points are in clauses 9 and 14. On clause 9, the limitation of liability as drafted is mutual in form but not in substance, because the carve-outs only operate in your favour. We have proposed symmetrical carve-outs.

On clause 14, we cannot accept the governing law as drafted. Our standard position is the courts of the jurisdiction in which the customer entity is registered, and in this case that is not negotiable for us.

Everything else is drafting preference and we will not hold up signature over it.

I am away from 19 to 26 May; my colleague Ravi Menon is copied and can progress matters in my absence.

Yours sincerely,
Eleanor Whitfield
General Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: legal

subject: Sub-processor list - objection under clause 6.3
body:
Hello,

We received your notice of 2 April adding a new sub-processor for transcription services.

Under clause 6.3 of our agreement we have 30 days to object to a new sub-processor on reasonable grounds. We are exercising that right. Our concern is that the named entity processes in a jurisdiction not covered by an adequacy decision, and our own regulator has been explicit with us about that category of transfer.

We are not asking you to drop the sub-processor for your other customers. We are asking whether our tenant can be excluded from that processing, or whether an alternative is available to us.

Please treat this as a formal objection under the agreement and confirm receipt.

Regards,
Ravi Menon
Legal Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: legal

subject: Clause 11.2 - clarification requested
body:
Extract under discussion:

  11.2  Either party may terminate this Agreement for material breach by
        written notice where such breach remains unremedied thirty (30)
        days after notice specifying the breach in reasonable detail.

Our question is procedural rather than substantive. The clause does not say what happens to data held on the platform during the 30 day remedy window if the breach alleged is non-payment. Does access continue through the window, or may it be suspended at day one under clause 7? Clauses 7 and 11.2 read together are ambiguous and we would like the position agreed in writing before signature.
label: legal

subject: Who signs this and on what authority
body: The document you sent needs signing by someone who can bind the company. Our finance director cannot -- the threshold in our articles is above the value here, so it has to go to a board member. Can you confirm on your side who is signing and in what capacity, so the file is complete if anyone ever asks?
label: legal

subject: Wording in section 4 does not match what we agreed
body: I have compared the document against my notes from the call on 12 March. We agreed the notice period would run from receipt, not from despatch. As drafted it runs from despatch, which shortens it by several days in practice. I would like it changed back to what we discussed before this goes any further.

subject: Can we say this publicly?

I have read the agreement twice and cannot tell whether that is permitted or needs your sign-off first. Could someone confirm in writing either way?

subject: Refund demand following the outage

We are invoking the service credit provision in schedule 3 following last month's outages. Our reading is that credits are due automatically and do not require a claim. Your team has told us verbally that a claim is required. We would like your position on the construction of schedule 3, in writing.
label: legal

subject: Vulnerability disclosure - our policy requires an agreement first
body: One of our researchers has found something in your platform. Before we tell you what it is, our disclosure policy requires a short agreement covering safe harbour and publication timing. This message is a request for that agreement, not the report itself -- the technical detail will follow once it is signed. Please route this to whoever can execute it.
label: legal

subject: Responsible disclosure - IDOR on the users endpoint
body: Changing the numeric id in the users endpoint returns records belonging to other tenants. No authentication bypass is needed, only a valid session. Requesting a security contact and a disclosure timeline.
label: security

subject: Phishing campaign impersonating your support team
body: Several of our staff received mail claiming to be your support desk, asking them to re-authenticate on a lookalike domain. The domain is registered this week and is not yours. Flagging so you can take it down and warn other customers.
label: security

subject: Suspected credential stuffing against our tenant
body: Your audit log shows roughly 4,000 failed sign-in attempts against our tenant overnight, spread across about 200 of our user accounts, from a wide range of addresses. Two accounts show a successful sign-in at the end of the run. We have locked both. We need to know what you can see from your side.
label: security

subject: RE: Our pen test findings affecting your platform
body:
Hi,

As agreed on the call, here is the summary of what our testers found that relates to your platform rather than to our own configuration.

There are two items. The first is that session cookies are issued without the SameSite attribute, which our testers rated medium. The second is that the password reset flow discloses whether an address is registered, through a difference in response timing rather than in the message text. That one they rated low but noted it is trivially automatable.

We are not publishing any of this. Our report goes to our board and to our insurer only. I would like to be able to tell them both that the items are acknowledged and have owners.

Is there a security contact I should be sending this to formally? At the moment it is going through our account manager, which does not feel right.

Thanks,
Mark Olsen
Platform Engineering, Initech
label: security

subject: Former employee still has access three weeks after leaving
body:
Hello,

We have a problem and I would like to understand how it happened.

A member of staff left us on 12 March. Our offboarding removed them from our directory the same day. This morning our audit review shows that account signing in to your platform on 28 March and again on 2 April, well after they left.

It appears the account was a local one in your system rather than a federated one, so removing them from our directory did nothing. If that is right then our entire offboarding assumption is wrong and there may be others.

Two things please. First, disable that account now. Second, give us a list of every account in our tenant that is local rather than federated, so we can audit the rest.

I am treating this as an incident on our side.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Operations, Contoso Ltd
label: security

subject: Question about your handling of a reported issue
body:
Dear team,

I reported an issue through your web form on 3 February. I received an automated acknowledgement and nothing since, despite a follow-up on 20 February.

To be clear about my intentions: I am not asking for a bounty, I have not published anything, and I do not intend to. But my own policy is 90 days from report to publication, and that date is approaching. I would much rather extend it than publish into a vacuum.

Could someone confirm the report was received by a human and give me a rough idea of timing? A single sentence would be enough.

Regards,
K. Lindqvist
label: security

subject: Odd entries in the activity log
body: Our admin log shows a role change on one of our accounts at 03:20 on Sunday, granting full administrative rights. Nobody on our team was working at that time and nobody has owned up to it. The account it was granted to is a service account we barely use. We have reverted the change. How do we find out where the request came from?
label: security

subject: #urgent thread

subject: Cannot log in - I think my password has been changed

I am raising this as a possible compromise rather than a simple lockout, because I would expect the reset to work if the account were merely locked. Please check whether the address on my account has been altered.
label: security

subject: GDPR breach notification obligations

We believe a misconfigured sharing link exposed a report containing customer records to anyone holding the URL, for roughly nine days. We need to establish the access log for that link before we can judge whether notification duties are triggered. Can you provide who retrieved it and when?

Thank you for getting back to me, and for the flexibility.

Tuesday and Thursday afternoon both work. Thursday is slightly better if there is a choice, as I have a commitment on Tuesday evening and would rather not be rushed.

Two questions if I may. First, will the technical stage be a live exercise or a discussion of previous work? I would prepare differently for each. Looking forward to it.

Best wishes,
Samuel Adeyemi

subject: New starter on the 14th - what is needed
body:
Morning,

We have a new analyst joining on the 14th and I want to get ahead of it this time, since the last one spent her first two days unable to do anything.

From my side I have raised the contract and the payroll record. What I need from you:

- A desk on the second floor, ideally near the rest of the team
- A laptop, standard analyst build

Helena Vos
People Operations

subject: Question about my final month

Before I raise the system access request I need to know which employment category contractors fall into for the purposes of our policy, because that determines what they are entitled to and whether the background check applies. The account setup itself I will handle separately.

subject: Complaint about a colleague's conduct in a customer meeting

But I am raising it here because the issue is the behaviour of a member of staff, not the customer relationship. I would like to know the process for raising a formal concern and whether it can be kept confidential from the person's line manager initially.

subject: Feature request: bulk edit on the records screen
body: It would save us a great deal of time if we could select several records and change the owner on all of them at once, rather than opening each one.
label: product_feedback

subject: The new dashboard is excellent
body: Just wanted to say the redesigned dashboard is a big improvement. The load time is noticeably better and putting the filters at the top was the right call. No complaints, for once.
label: product_feedback

subject: Thoughts after three months of use
body:
Hi Jane,

You asked for honest feedback at the end of the quarter, so here it is.

What works well: the import is genuinely painless, and the permissions model is the first one I have used that our non-technical managers can actually understand without training.

What does not: the reporting screen is built for someone who already knows what they are looking for. There is no way to browse. Every one of our new starters has asked the same question in their first week, which tells you something.

The thing I would change first is smaller than either of those. When you delete something there is no undo, only a confirmation dialog, and people click through dialogs. One undo would prevent most of the support requests we raise with you.

Happy to talk any of this through.

Regards,
Sarah Chen
Head of Operations, Umbrella Retail
label: product_feedback

subject: RE: Beta invitation - feedback on the new editor
body:
Hello,

Thanks for including us in the beta. We have had four people using the new editor for a fortnight.

Overall it is faster and the keyboard shortcuts are a real improvement. Two of the four said they would not want to go back.

The other two struggled, and the reason is consistent: the autosave indicator is too subtle. Both of them lost work, or believed they had, because they could not tell whether a change had been committed. One of them started copying everything into a text file before editing, which rather defeats the point.

I would not hold the release for the things in the first paragraph. I would hold it for the autosave indicator.

Best,
Tomas Berg
Operations Director, Globex Industries
label: product_feedback

subject: #general thread
body: is there a reason the date filter defaults to last 7 days every single time you open it? every person on my team changes it to last 30 first thing, every morning. remembering it would be such a small thing but honestly it's the thing that annoys me most about using this.
label: product_feedback

subject: An observation about the mobile view
body: Nothing is broken, so this is not a fault report. But the action buttons on the record screen sit below the fold on a phone, so you have to scroll past the whole record to do anything with it. On a laptop they are the first thing you see. It makes the phone version feel like an afterthought even though everything works.
label: product_feedback

subject: What we ended up building ourselves
body: For your information rather than as a request. We have written a small internal tool that pulls from your API every night and produces a weekly summary by team, because there is no way to get that view out of the product. It took about two days. I mention it because if we needed it, others probably do, and we would happily throw ours away.
label: product_feedback

subject: Export is broken for large accounts
body: I have called this broken but I want to be fair -- it does complete, eventually. For our largest account the export takes upwards of eleven minutes, during which the screen gives no indication that anything is happening. People assume it has failed and start it again, which makes it worse. The function works; the experience of using it is what I am complaining about.
label: product_feedback

subject: Pricing page is confusing
body: To be clear I am not asking for a quote and I am not a prospect -- we have been a customer for two years. I am telling you that your pricing page is hard to follow, because three of my colleagues read it and came away with three different understandings of what a seat is. If it confuses existing customers it is presumably costing you sales too.
label: product_feedback

subject: Security question that is really a usability one
body: Our security team insists on 20 character passwords and re-authentication every four hours. Your product honours both, so nothing is wrong. The consequence is that people leave the tab open all day to avoid signing in again, which is worse for security than the policy is good. A 'remember this device' option would solve it. This is a design comment, not a vulnerability.
label: product_feedback

subject: Add five users to our workspace

label: account_admin

subject: Reset multi-factor authentication for a user

subject: RE: Role changes after the reorganisation
body:
Hi,

Following our reorganisation on 1 April the reporting lines have changed and the roles in your platform no longer reflect who does what.

Specifically: the four people previously in the Northern team now report into Operations and need the Operations role rather than Regional. Two of them also need the approver permission, which they did not have before.

I can do the role change myself in the admin console. What I cannot work out is the approver permission -- I can see the toggle but it is greyed out for me, presumably because I do not hold it myself.

Could you either grant it to the two named in the attached list, or grant me the ability to do it so I am not raising this with you every time we reshuffle?

Thanks,
Helena Vos
People Operations
label: account_admin

subject: Single sign-on rollout - a question about existing accounts
body:
Good morning,

We are enabling single sign-on next month and I want to understand what happens to accounts that already exist.

Our situation is that about 60 users were created directly in your platform over the last two years, before we had a directory worth federating. Their addresses match our directory, but the accounts are local.

When we turn SSO on, do those accounts link automatically on the basis of the matching address, or do they become orphaned and need recreating? If it is the latter I need to plan for it, because recreating 60 accounts loses their saved views.

I would rather find this out now than on the morning of the cutover.

Regards,
Mark Olsen
Platform Engineering, Initech
label: account_admin

subject: Deactivating accounts without deleting the history
body:
Hello,

A question about how to remove people properly.

When someone leaves we currently delete their account. We have discovered that this also removes their name from the history of everything they touched, so records now show actions taken by 'Unknown user'. Our auditors were not impressed.

Is there a way to deactivate an account so that the person can no longer sign in but their name is retained on past activity? If there is I cannot find it, and if there is not, what do other customers do?

Thanks,
Priya Patel
Accounts Payable, Northwind Trading
label: account_admin

subject: #help thread
body: one of our team can see the reports tab and another can't, and as far as i can tell they're set up identically. same team, same job. what determines whether that tab shows up? i've compared the two side by side and can't spot the difference.

subject: We have run out
body: Trying to add someone this morning and it will not let me -- it says we have reached the limit. We are apparently at 50 of 50. I do not need to buy more yet, because two of the fifty left the company in February and should not still be counted. How do I free those up?

subject: Wrong address on my profile

I have changed it in our own directory but it has not carried through. Can it be updated at your end, and will the old entries update too?

subject: Suspicious login from an unknown location

What I would like is to add that location to an allow list, or turn off the alert for that user, because we have had four of these this month and people are starting to ignore them.
label: account_admin

subject: Charged for users we cannot see
body: Our invoice is for 62 seats. The admin console lists 55 people. I have raised this with finance and they have pointed me back here, because their view is that the invoice reflects whatever your system reports and the discrepancy must be in the user list rather than in the billing. So my question is where the other seven are -- are there accounts that count towards the total but do not appear in the list I can see?
label: account_admin

subject: Delivery for order 55120 has not arrived
body: Order 55120 was due on Tuesday and has not arrived. The tracking page has shown 'in transit' for six days with no movement. Can you chase the carrier?
label: logistics

subject: Return of damaged hardware
body: Two of the twelve units in the last shipment arrived with crushed casings. We would like to return both for replacement. Please send a returns label and let us know whether to ship them back together.
label: logistics

subject: Customs paperwork missing for the Rotterdam shipment
body: The consignment is being held at Rotterdam because the commercial invoice does not show the commodity code. The broker needs a corrected document before it can clear.
label: logistics

subject: RE: Delivery schedule for the Q3 rollout
body:
Hi,

Thanks for the draft schedule. A few things from our side before we lock it in.

The dates themselves are fine with one exception: the week of 12 August is our warehouse stock take and we cannot receive anything that week. Nothing at all, I am afraid -- the team is fully committed to the count.

Second, please split the delivery by site rather than sending everything to head office. Last time we received the lot here and had to redistribute it ourselves, which cost us the better part of a week and some damage in transit that was entirely our own doing.

Third, our goods-in closes at 15:00, not 17:00 as your carrier seems to assume. Two deliveries were refused last quarter for arriving late in the day.

Site addresses are on the attached sheet.

Regards,
Tomas Berg
Operations Director, Globex Industries
label: logistics

subject: Lead times before we commit to the order
body:
Good afternoon,

We are close to raising the purchase order but the lead time you quoted has moved twice and I need something firm before I can sign it off.

The original quote said 4 to 6 weeks. The revised one says 8 to 10. Our project has a fixed installation window in October and an 10 week lead time from today puts us right at the edge of it.

Could you tell me, honestly, what the realistic figure is at the moment? If it is 10 weeks I would rather know now and plan for it than be told in September. If there is an option to expedite part of the order -- even just the first site -- I would like to price that.

Thanks,
Daniel Fischer
Procurement Lead, Vandelay Group
label: logistics

subject: Wrong items in shipment 8841
body:
Hello,

Shipment 8841 arrived this morning. The quantities are right but two of the line items are not what we ordered.

We ordered 20 of the 1.5 metre cables and received 20 of the 3 metre. We also ordered 4 rack shelves and received 4 rack rails, which are not interchangeable.

We can use the longer cables, so if it is simpler for everyone we will keep those and settle the price difference. The rails are no use to us at all and will need to go back.

The packing note matches what we ordered, so I suspect this is a picking error rather than an order entry one.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Operations, Contoso Ltd
label: logistics

subject: #warehouse thread
body: the pallet that was supposed to come friday still isn't here and the driver who came monday said he had nothing for us. we've got the install team booked for thursday and nothing to install. can someone find out where it actually is
label: logistics

subject: Can you hold these until September
body: Our new site is not ready -- the building work has slipped by about six weeks. We do not want the units sitting in a corridor and we have nowhere secure to put them. Is it possible for you to keep them until we are ready, and does that cost anything?
label: logistics

subject: Invoice received before the goods
body: We have an invoice dated the 2nd for a consignment that has not turned up. Finance will not pay against goods we have not received, which is fair enough. My question is not really about the invoice though -- I want to know where the consignment is, because the invoice being issued suggests it left you. Has it shipped?
label: logistics

subject: Damaged on arrival - is this a warranty claim?
body: A unit arrived with a cracked front panel. I am unsure whether to raise this as a warranty matter or a delivery one, so I am starting here. The outer carton was visibly crushed on one corner, which makes me think it happened in transit rather than being a manufacturing fault. If that changes who handles it, please redirect me.
label: logistics

subject: Reseller agreement enquiry
body: We are a systems integrator in the Nordics and would like to resell your product to our existing client base. Who handles reseller agreements and what are the requirements?
label: partnerships

subject: Technology integration proposal
body: We build workflow automation software and several mutual customers have asked for an integration between our products. We would like to discuss building and listing one.
label: partnerships

subject: Co-marketing at the autumn conference
body: We are exhibiting at the industry conference in October and wondered whether you would be interested in a joint stand and a shared session, splitting the cost.
label: partnerships

subject: RE: Referral arrangement - where we got to
body:
Hi Jane,

Picking this up again after the summer.

To recap where we left it: we send you leads in the manufacturing sector where our own product does not fit, and you pay a referral fee on anything that closes. We had broadly agreed 10% of first year value.

The two things we did not resolve were attribution and duration. On attribution, we need a mechanism that does not rely on the customer remembering to mention us -- a form or a tracked introduction, something auditable. On duration, you proposed 6 months from introduction and we proposed 12; I suspect we land at 9.

I have a slot with our commercial director on the 21st and would like to take him a near-final position. Can we speak before then?

Best,
Sarah Chen
Head of Operations, Umbrella Retail
label: partnerships

subject: Joining your integration directory - what is involved
body:
Hello,

We have built an integration against your public API and have about thirty mutual customers using it. We would like it listed in your directory.

Looking at your listing requirements I have some questions:

- The certification checklist mentions a security review. Is that a questionnaire or an actual test against our system?
- It also requires support for the newer authentication flow. We currently use the older one. Is the older one going to be withdrawn, and if so when? That affects whether we invest in migrating now or later.
- Is there a fee for listing?

The integration itself is stable and has been in production for over a year, so this is about the listing process rather than the engineering.

Regards,
Mark Olsen
Platform Engineering, Initech
label: partnerships

subject: Working together in a market neither of us covers
body: We keep meeting your people at the same tenders in the public sector, usually on opposite sides. It occurred to me that we lose those bids to the same competitor more often than we lose them to each other. I wonder whether there is a version of this where we bid together rather than apart. Worth a conversation?
label: partnerships

subject: Introduction from a mutual customer
body: Contoso suggested I get in touch. They use both our products side by side and spend a lot of effort moving data between them by hand. Their view is that the two of us talking would save them that work and probably save it for others in the same position. I am happy to set something up if there is interest at your end.
label: partnerships

subject: Volume pricing for our clients
body: This will read like a purchasing enquiry but we would not be the end user. We manage IT for about forty small firms and would be buying on their behalf, under our own paper, with our own support wrapped around it. That is a different arrangement from a bulk discount and probably needs a different kind of agreement. Who should I be speaking to?
label: partnerships

subject: Can we use your logo
body: We would like to display your logo on our website to show that we integrate with you. I appreciate there is a trademark question in here and I am happy to sign whatever brand guidelines you have. But the underlying question is whether you want partners promoting the integration at all, which is a commercial decision rather than a legal one. What is your position?
label: partnerships

subject: Our integration broke after your release
body: Our connector stopped working after your release on the 14th -- a field was renamed without notice. I have raised the technical detail through support separately. What I am raising here is that as a listed partner we were not told, and the release notes did not mention it. The fault is fixable in an afternoon; the process that let it reach us unannounced is the thing I want to discuss.
label: partnerships

subject: Interview request for a feature article
body: I am a reporter writing a feature on workflow software for a trade publication. Would your CEO be available for a 30 minute interview in the next fortnight?
label: press

subject: Comment on the industry report published today
body: An analyst report published this morning names your company. We are running a piece this afternoon and would like a comment. Our deadline is 16:00.
label: press

subject: RE: Briefing under embargo - confirming the terms
body:
Hi Jane,

Thanks for offering the briefing ahead of the announcement.

To confirm what I can and cannot do, so there is no misunderstanding later: I am happy to hold until 09:00 on the 14th. I cannot agree to copy approval, and I cannot agree not to seek comment from others in the market -- our editorial policy does not allow either. If those are conditions of the briefing then I will have to decline and cover it on the day like everyone else.

If the embargo alone is acceptable, I am free Tuesday or Wednesday morning.

One thing I would find genuinely useful is a customer willing to speak on the record. Announcements without one tend to get a couple of paragraphs; with one they get a proper piece.

Best,
R. Castellano
Technology Correspondent
label: press

subject: Fact check ahead of publication
body:
Hello,

I am publishing tomorrow morning and want to give you the chance to correct anything factual before I do.

The piece states that your company was founded in 2016, has around 200 employees, and raised a funding round last year. It also says you have customers in the public sector, which I have from a published case study on your own site.

If any of that is wrong, please tell me what the correct figure is. If you would rather not comment on any of it, that is your right and I will note that you were approached.

I am not able to share the full text before publication.

Deadline is 18:00 today.

Regards,
R. Castellano
Technology Correspondent
label: press

subject: Writing something about the sector
body: I am putting together a piece on how firms in this space handle the transition to subscription pricing. I am not looking to make anyone look bad, and I am happy to keep individual figures out of it. Is there someone at your end who could talk me through how you approached it? Background rather than quotable, if that is easier to agree to.
label: press

subject: Your founder's talk last week
body: I watched the recording of the conference talk and there was a point about how you handle data residency that I would like to explore further. I write for an industry newsletter with a few thousand readers. Would she be willing to expand on that, either on a call or in writing? I can send questions in advance.
label: press

subject: Working to a deadline this afternoon
body: I am running a short piece at four o'clock and it mentions your company in passing. I would rather include your side than say you did not respond. Two sentences would be plenty. Is there someone who can turn that round quickly, or should I note that no one was available?
label: press

subject: Questions about the outage last Thursday
body: I understand the technical details will have been dealt with through your support channels and I am not asking to reopen those. I am a journalist, and I am writing about the outage because several of your customers have posted publicly about it. My questions are about cause, duration and what customers were told, and I need a response by Friday.
label: press

subject: Following up on a data exposure claim
body: A researcher has told us they reported an issue to you in February and had no response. I am not reporting the vulnerability myself and I have no technical details to pass on. I am asking whether you received such a report, what happened to it, and whether any customer data was affected. If there is a security contact who should answer this rather than a press one, please forward it.
label: press

subject: Request for your published financial figures
body: This may look like an information request for your compliance or finance team and I am happy to be redirected. I am a reporter compiling a sector comparison from published accounts. I already have your filed figures; what I want is someone who can explain the year on year change in one particular line, on the record, before I publish next week.
label: press

subject: Air conditioning not working on the third floor
body: The air conditioning on the third floor has been off since Monday and the room is uncomfortably warm. Please arrange for someone to look at it.
label: facilities

subject: Booking the large meeting room for the quarterly review
body: Could the large meeting room be reserved for the whole of 14 June, with the partition opened and seating for forty?
label: facilities

subject: RE: Desk moves for the new team layout
body:
Hi,

Thanks for the floor plan. It mostly works but there are three problems.

First, the plan puts the support team next to the main door. They are on calls all day and that is the noisiest spot on the floor. Could they swap with the finance group, who are quieter and would not mind the traffic?

Second, there are 14 desks marked for a team of 16. Two people would have nowhere to sit.

Third, the standing desks currently on the second floor need to come with the people who use them -- they were provided on medical grounds and cannot simply be reassigned to whoever ends up at that position.

If the moves happen over a weekend that would be much less disruptive than doing it midweek.

Thanks,
Helena Vos
People Operations
label: facilities

subject: Cleaning contract - quality has dropped
body:
Good morning,

I want to raise something before it becomes a formal complaint.

Since the cleaning contractor changed in January the standard has fallen noticeably. The specific issues are the kitchens, which are not being done daily as the specification requires, and the glass in the meeting rooms, which has not been done at all as far as anyone can tell.

I have logged four individual reports through the portal since February and had no response to any of them, which is honestly the more concerning part.

Could we have a review meeting with the contractor present? I would rather fix this than escalate it.

Regards,
Priya Patel
Accounts Payable, Northwind Trading
label: facilities

subject: Parking allocation for the new site
body:
Hello,

The new building has 30 spaces for roughly 90 staff and I need an allocation policy before we move in, because the current arrangement of first come first served will not survive contact with reality.

Things I know we have to accommodate: three blue badge holders, two people who carry equipment to customer sites most days, and the pool car.

Beyond that I do not have a strong view and would rather follow whatever has worked elsewhere. Is there a policy from the other sites I can adapt rather than invent one?

There is also a question of whether we can rent additional spaces in the multi-storey next door, and what that would cost.

Thanks,
Helena Vos
People Operations
label: facilities

subject: #office thread
body: the tap in the second floor kitchen has been dripping for about two weeks and it's getting worse, there's now a puddle under the counter in the mornings. who do i tell about that? i've mentioned it to two people and nothing has happened.
label: facilities

subject: Somewhere to take calls
body: Since the move to the open plan layout there is nowhere quiet to take a private conversation. People are using the stairwell, which is neither private nor comfortable. Could a couple of the small meeting rooms be left unbookable for exactly this, or could booths be put in? It comes up at every team meeting.
label: facilities

subject: The card readers on the side entrance
body: The reader on the side entrance rejects about one in three attempts and everyone has got into the habit of going round to the front instead, which adds a few minutes each way. It has been like this since before Christmas. It is not urgent but it is a daily irritation for about thirty people.
label: facilities

subject: Door access not working for a new starter
body: Our new analyst started Monday and her building pass does not open anything. I realise access rights sound like an IT matter but this is the physical card for the doors, not a system login -- her system accounts are all fine. The card was ordered with two weeks notice so I am not sure what went wrong.
label: facilities

subject: Equipment for a member of staff returning from leave
body: Someone is coming back from long term sick leave next month and occupational health has recommended a specific chair and a sit-stand desk. There is an HR dimension to this and HR are aware, but the thing I actually need is the equipment ordered, installed and in place before her first day. Who arranges that and what is the lead time?
label: facilities

subject: SOC 2 report request for our annual audit
body: Our auditors have asked for your most recent SOC 2 Type II report. Could you send it, along with the bridge letter covering the period since the report date?
label: compliance

subject: ISO 27001 certificate and scope statement
body: Please provide your current ISO 27001 certificate and the scope statement showing which entities and services are covered by it.
label: compliance

subject: Annual policy attestation outstanding
body: Four members of your team have not completed the annual information security policy attestation. The deadline was 31 March. Please confirm when these will be completed.
label: compliance

subject: RE: Evidence request for the internal audit
body:
Hi,

Thanks for the documents sent last week. Our internal audit team has been through them and has come back with three gaps.

First, the access review evidence covers the second half of the year only. They need both halves to evidence the control operated throughout the period.

Second, the change management sample they selected includes two changes with no recorded approver. That may be a records issue rather than a control failure, but we need an explanation either way.

Third, the business continuity test report is dated but not signed, and they will not accept it unsigned.

None of this is a finding yet. It becomes one if we cannot close it before the exit meeting on the 30th.

I appreciate this is tedious. It is however the difference between a clean report and a qualified one.

Regards,
Daniel Fischer
Procurement Lead, Vandelay Group
label: compliance

subject: Control questionnaire - responses needed before renewal
body:
Good morning,

Our regulator requires us to assess material outsourced providers annually, and you are in scope this year.

The questionnaire is attached. It is long and I am sorry about that; most of it will be answerable from your existing certifications. The sections that usually need a written answer are:

- Section 4, on how you segregate customer data in a shared environment
- Section 7, on your incident notification timescales and what triggers them
- Section 11, on your own oversight of the sub-providers you depend on

We need it back within 30 days. If any answer is "we do not do this", please say so plainly rather than leaving it blank -- a gap we know about is manageable, a gap we discover later is not.

Regards,
Eleanor Whitfield
General Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: compliance

subject: Records retention - are we meeting the requirement
body:
Hello,

We have a regulatory obligation to retain certain records for seven years in a form that cannot be altered after the fact.

Our understanding is that your platform retains the audit trail indefinitely but allows an administrator to delete records, including their history. If that is right then we do not meet the requirement using your product alone, and we need to either change how we use it or export to somewhere immutable.

Before I take this to our risk committee I want to be sure I have the facts right. Could you confirm, in writing:

1. Whether an administrator can delete a record together with its history
2. Whether that deletion is itself logged, and where
3. Whether any retention lock or legal hold feature exists

Thanks,
Ravi Menon
Legal Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: compliance

subject: Our auditors are asking about you
body: We are in the middle of our annual review and the people doing it want to know how we satisfy ourselves that you are doing what you say you are. I do not think they want anything from you directly at this stage -- they want to see what we hold on file. What do you normally give customers for this, and is there anything you publish that I can point them at?
label: compliance

subject: Something we have to be able to demonstrate
body: We have to be able to show, on demand, who approved each change to a customer record and when. Not who made it -- who approved it. At the moment I can show who made it. If the approval is recorded somewhere I cannot find it, and if it is not recorded then we have a problem we need to solve before our next review.
label: compliance

subject: Contract clause on audit rights
body: Our agreement gives us a right to audit, and our lawyers have confirmed it is validly drafted, so this is not a legal question. The practical question is how that right is exercised: what notice you expect, whether you accept a questionnaire in place of an on-site visit, and whether you have a standard process. We would rather follow your process than invent one.
label: compliance

subject: Reporting a control failure we found ourselves
body: I want to flag something before you hear it elsewhere. During our own testing we found that one of our administrators had retained elevated rights for four months after changing role. Nothing was misused -- we have checked the logs thoroughly and there is no security incident here. But the control did not operate as designed, and our agreement requires us to tell you about control failures affecting shared processes.
label: compliance

subject: Supplier onboarding questionnaire
body: Before we can raise a purchase order you need to complete our supplier onboarding pack: company details, bank verification, insurance certificates and the modern slavery statement.
label: procurement

subject: Invitation to tender - closing 30 June
body: We are running a competitive tender for workflow software and would like to invite you to participate. The documents are attached and responses close at noon on 30 June.
label: procurement

subject: Purchase order 4500128833 raised
body: Purchase order 4500128833 has been raised against your quotation QT-9912. Please quote the PO number on all invoices or they will be rejected by our ledger.
label: procurement

subject: RE: Vendor review before renewal
body:
Hi Jane,

Our policy requires a formal review of any supplier above a spend threshold before renewal, and you are over it this year for the first time.

The review is not adversarial. It is three things: confirmation that the commercial terms remain competitive, evidence that the service has performed against what was agreed, and a check that the supplier record is current.

For the second of those I need your view on the two service credits we claimed in the last twelve months. My own record says both were agreed and applied, but I would like that confirmed so the file is complete.

For the third, your insurance certificate on file expired in April and the bank details we hold have not been re-verified in two years. Both will need refreshing.

If we can close these out by the end of the month the renewal goes through on the nod. If not it goes to committee, which adds six weeks.

Regards,
Daniel Fischer
Procurement Lead, Vandelay Group
label: procurement

subject: Quotation required in a specific format
body:
Good afternoon,

Thanks for the pricing you sent. Unfortunately I cannot put it through our system in the form it is in.

Our purchasing platform needs each line as a separate item with a unit price and a quantity. Your quotation gives a single bundled figure with the components listed underneath in prose. Finance will not accept it and I cannot split it myself without guessing at your internal pricing.

Could you reissue it itemised? Specifically I need the licence component, the implementation component and the support component priced separately, each with a quantity and a unit price.

The total can stay exactly as you have quoted it -- I am not trying to renegotiate, I just need it in a form our system will swallow.

Thanks,
Priya Patel
Accounts Payable, Northwind Trading
label: procurement

subject: Before we can set you up
body: We cannot pay anyone who is not on our approved supplier list, and you are not on it yet. Getting on it takes about three weeks and needs several documents from you. I would start this now rather than when the first invoice arrives, because otherwise the invoice sits unpaid and everyone gets annoyed. Who at your end handles this sort of paperwork?
label: procurement

subject: Comparing three offers
body: I have three responses in front of me and I am trying to compare them fairly. Yours is the only one that prices implementation separately, which makes your headline figure look lower and your total look higher. Before I put this to the panel, can you confirm whether your implementation figure is a fixed price or an estimate, because the other two have folded theirs in as fixed.
label: procurement

subject: Contract terms we cannot accept
body: Our legal team has looked at your standard terms and will not sign them, but that is not really what I am writing about. Under our own rules, a supplier who will not accept our standard terms has to go through an exceptions process before any order can be placed, regardless of who is right on the substance. I need to know now whether you will move, because the exceptions process takes five weeks and I have to start it today if it is needed.
label: procurement

subject: Insurance certificate and audit evidence
body: I need your employers liability and professional indemnity certificates. I realise you supply audit evidence to a different team and there may be an overlap, but this is not for an audit -- it is for the supplier file, and without current certificates the record lapses and the payment run drops you. The certificates we hold expired in April.
label: procurement

subject: Why was this bought without us
body: A department has been using your product for eight months on a departmental card and it has only now come to light. I am not blaming you -- you sold to someone who said they could buy. But it has to be regularised: brought onto a proper contract, a purchase order raised, and the card payments stopped. What do you need from us to convert an existing account onto a purchase order arrangement?
label: procurement

subject: Onboarding session for twelve new users
body: We have twelve people joining the platform next month and would like to book an onboarding session for them. What do you offer and what does it cost?
label: training

subject: Administrator certification course
body: Two of our staff would like to take the administrator certification. Could you send the course dates, the prerequisites and the exam arrangements?
label: training

subject: RE: Enablement plan for the wider rollout
body:
Hi Jane,

Following our conversation about extending the rollout from the pilot team to the whole division.

The pilot went well, but I think that is partly because the pilot group were volunteers who wanted it to work. The next 200 people did not ask for this and some of them will actively resist it.

So what I want from the enablement plan is less product walkthrough and more "here is what changes about your day". The pilot group needed about two hours of training. I suspect this group needs less training and more reassurance.

Practically:
- Can sessions be recorded? Shift workers cannot all attend live.
- Do you have material aimed at people who are not choosing to adopt this?
- Is there a train-the-trainer option? Twelve sessions delivered by you is expensive; four delivered by you to our own trainers is not.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Head of Operations, Umbrella Retail
label: training

subject: Documentation gaps we keep hitting
body:
Hello,

This is a request for material rather than a complaint, though it has grown out of some frustration.

Our team has now asked support the same three questions repeatedly, and each time the answer is helpful but exists nowhere we can find it ourselves. The three are: how permissions inherit when a team is nested, what exactly happens to records when a user is deactivated, and how the import handles duplicates.

Each of those has an answer. None of them is in the documentation, or if it is, it is not where anyone looks.

Would you consider writing them up? I would happily review drafts, since we have hit every edge case in all three.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Operations, Contoso Ltd
label: training

subject: People are not using it properly
body: Six months in and about half the team are still doing things the old way alongside the new system, which gives us the worst of both. When I ask why, the answer is usually that they were shown once at the beginning and never felt confident. I do not think this is a product problem. What do other customers do at this stage?
label: training

subject: Something for people to refer back to
body: The session you ran in March was good and people said so at the time. The difficulty is that three months later nobody remembers the detail, and there is nothing to go back to except their own notes. Is there a written version of what was covered, or a recording, or anything we could put on our intranet?
label: training

subject: #team thread
body: new starter question -- is there anywhere that explains how the approval chain actually works end to end? i've been shown bits of it by three different people and they don't entirely agree with each other. would rather learn it properly once than keep guessing
label: training

subject: The product is too complicated
body: I could file this as product feedback and perhaps I should. But before I do, I want to rule out the possibility that we simply do not know how to use it. Three people here find the reporting module impenetrable. If that is a design problem I will send feedback. If it is a knowledge problem then what we need is someone to show us, and I would rather find that out first.
label: training

subject: New starter cannot do anything
body: Our new analyst has her account and her permissions are correct -- I have checked them against a colleague's and they match. The problem is she does not know what to do with it. I do not need an access change, I need whatever you give people at the start. Is there a self-service path for a single new joiner, or does it have to be a booked session?
label: training

subject: Security awareness for our administrators
body: Our security team wants our platform administrators to understand the consequences of the permissions they hand out -- not security in general, which we cover internally, but specifically what each role in your product can actually reach. Is there material aimed at administrators on that, or is it something your security people would need to put together?
label: training

subject: Subject access request
body: I am making a subject access request under the GDPR for all personal data you hold about me. Please confirm receipt and respond within one month.
label: data_privacy

subject: Erasure request for a former customer
body: A former customer has asked us to delete their personal data. Some of it sits in your platform as our processor. Please confirm the process for deletion and how you evidence it.
label: data_privacy

subject: RE: Data residency for our European entity
body:
Hello,

Our European entity has a requirement that personal data of its customers is stored within the EU and not transferred outside it except under an approved mechanism.

Reading your documentation I can establish that primary storage is in the region we select. What I cannot establish is what happens to:

- Backups, and whether they stay in region
- Support access, and whether your support staff outside the EU can view customer records
- Any processing by sub-processors for things like search indexing or transcription

The third of those is where I expect the problem to be, based on your published sub-processor list.

I am not asking you to change anything. I am asking for an accurate description so we can assess it properly, and if transfers do occur, which mechanism you rely on.

Regards,
Ravi Menon
Legal Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: data_privacy

subject: Retention periods do not match our policy
body:
Good afternoon,

We have completed a review of what your platform retains and for how long, and there is a mismatch with our own retention policy.

Our policy requires deletion of customer contact records 24 months after the relationship ends. Your platform appears to retain them indefinitely unless deleted manually, and the deleted items area holds them for a further 90 days after that.

Two questions. First, is there a configurable retention period we have missed? Second, if there is not, does the 90 day deleted items window count as processing for our purposes, or is it a technical backup we can disregard? Our DPO's view is that it counts.

If there is no configuration option then we will need to build a scheduled deletion against your API, which we would rather not do.

Regards,
Eleanor Whitfield
General Counsel, Vandelay Group
label: data_privacy

subject: Consent records for the marketing list
body:
Hi,

We are cleaning up our marketing list and have found we cannot evidence consent for a large part of it.

Specifically, about 4,000 contacts were imported from a spreadsheet in 2021. The import recorded the date but not the source, so we cannot show where the consent came from or what people were told at the time.

Our position is that we cannot rely on consent we cannot evidence, so those contacts need to come out or be re-permissioned.

What I need from you is a way to identify exactly which records came from that import, since the batch reference does not appear to be exposed anywhere in the interface. If it is stored but not shown, an export would do.

Thanks,
Helena Vos
People Operations
label: data_privacy

subject: A customer wants to know what we have on them
body: Someone has written in asking for a copy of everything we hold about them. I know we have a month to respond. What I do not know is how to get it out of your system in a form I can actually send them -- the export gives me internal identifiers and references to other records rather than something a person could read.
label: data_privacy

subject: Who can see the notes field
body: Our staff write free text notes against customer records, and some of what goes in there is fairly personal -- health circumstances, financial difficulty, that sort of thing. I need to know exactly which roles can read that field, whether it appears in exports, and whether it is included when a record is shared externally. If the answer is 'anyone with access to the record' then we need to change how we use it.
label: data_privacy

subject: Removing someone completely
body: A person has asked us to remove them entirely. I have deleted the main record. But their name still appears in the history of other records, in the notes of a colleague's entries, and in an export somebody scheduled last year. I am not confident that deleting the record actually achieves what they asked for. What else is there and how do I reach it?
label: data_privacy

subject: Possible exposure of customer records
body: A sharing link was left open longer than it should have been and we are working out whether personal data was accessible through it. Our security team is handling the technical side and has the access logs. What I need is separate: whether this meets the threshold for notifying our regulator and the individuals, which depends on what data the link actually exposed. Can you tell me precisely which fields a holder of that link could see?
label: data_privacy

subject: Sub-processor added without notice
body: Our agreement requires 30 days notice of a new sub-processor and I am told our objection rights are a contractual matter for our legal team. Understood. My concern is narrower and it is a data protection one: the new sub-processor appears in your published list with a start date that has already passed, which means processing has begun. I need to know what categories of personal data have been shared with them, and since when.
label: data_privacy
